business.what_we_do: A neighbourhood sourdough bakery in a small river town. We bake naturally leavened bread every morning and teach weekend baking classes for home bakers.

audience.who: People within a few miles who care about good bread, plus home bakers anywhere who want to understand sourdough well enough to stop following recipes blindly.
problems: Their home loaves come out dense and they do not know why
They think good bread needs equipment they do not own
They are unsure which supermarket 'sourdough' is real
questions_they_ask: How do I know when the dough has proofed enough?
Can I bake good bread in a normal oven?
How do I keep a starter alive when I travel?

by_platform.instagram: Locals and home bakers who save posts to try at the weekend.
by_platform.facebook: Neighbours: opening hours, specials, class dates.
by_platform.linkedin: Other small food business owners curious how a bakery runs.

pillars.name: How bread actually works
pillars.about: The why behind fermentation, hydration, heat and time, in plain words.

pillars.name: Fix my loaf
pillars.about: One common home-baking problem, one cause, one fix.

pillars.name: Behind the counter
pillars.about: What a working bakery day looks like, including the things that go wrong.

pillars.name: Bake with us
pillars.about: Weekend classes: what people learn and what they take home.

offers.name: Starter feeding card
offers.what: A one-page card: how to feed and keep a sourdough starter.
offers.call_to_action: Ask for a feeding card at the counter

offers.name: Weekly bread subscription
offers.what: One loaf a week, reserved, collected Friday or Saturday.

offers.name: Saturday sourdough class
offers.what: A four-hour hands-on class for eight people. You leave with a loaf, a starter and a one-page method.

offers.name: Private bake day
offers.what: A full day in the bakery for a team or a group of friends, up to twelve people.
offers.call_to_action: Ask about a private bake day

voice.register: Warm, plain and specific. Sounds like a baker talking across the counter: short sentences, real quantities, no romance about flour.
do: Give the number: grams, hours, degrees
Explain the why before the how
Admit what went wrong in our own bakes
signature_phrases: Watch the dough, not the clock

person.note: Ava speaks from her own bench: what she tried, what failed, what she does now.

company.note: Talks to the neighbour: what is fresh, what is on, how to join in.

compliance.disclaimer: We bake with wheat, rye, milk, eggs, nuts and sesame in one kitchen.

known_for.value: the bakery that takes two days

core_belief.value: Bread should take two days, not two hours.

contrarian.value: Sourdough is a process, not a flavour.
contrarian.experience: Years of customers asking for 'the sour one'.

for.experience: Our loaves sell out because people taste the difference.

against.experience: We tried frozen dough once, in our first month.

differentiation.us: start the dough two days ahead

non_negotiables.value: show real hands and real ovens

catalyst.value: Every bakery on the high street sold the same frozen loaf.

core_truth.value: Time is the ingredient nobody can fake.

proof.value: Two-day dough, every loaf, since the day we opened.

myths.value: You need special flour to start.

steps_to_result.value: Feed the starter at the same time each day.
Mix the dough the evening before.
